edges.description: Impaired heme O synthase reduces production of the precursor required for heme A.
Limited heme A availability impairs maturation of the heme-containing COX complex.
Reduced functional COX lowers capacity for electron transfer from cytochrome c to oxygen.
Reduced COX-dependent proton translocation can restrict oxidative ATP production.
Mitochondrial dysfunction is associated with destructive white-matter lesions in COX10-associated Leigh disease; the intervening cellular sequence is unresolved.
Respiratory-chain dysfunction contributes to muscle disease.
Cardiac involvement can accompany COX10 deficiency.
Mitochondrial dysfunction can affect renal tubular function.
Impaired oxidative metabolism can favor lactate accumulation; lactic acidosis is not demonstrated in every genotype-confirmed case.
White-matter degeneration underlies the leukodystrophic presentation.
Diffuse CNS injury contributes to progressive neurologic dysfunction.
White-matter tract injury can contribute to pyramidal motor dysfunction.
CNS involvement can impair cognition and development.
Cerebellar and connecting white-matter injury can contribute to ataxia.
The patient-derived cellular system has reduced mature COX without accumulating assembly intermediates.
